How can I sell a house fast in Seattle?

You have three practical routes in Seattle: list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. Speed depends on the condition of the house, whether tenants live in it, and how much you will spend on repairs first.

Seattle is a big city with a high price tag. The Census Bureau estimates 784,777 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 737,015 in the 2020 census. Only 43.7 percent of Seattle homes are owner-occupied, compared with 65.2 percent nationally.

Here is how the city looks in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures:

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $938,600, against $332,700 for the country as a whole.
  • Median gross rent: $2,030 a month.
  • Median household income: $123,860.
  • Households: 363,466, averaging 2.00 people each.
  • Mean commute to work: 26.0 minutes.

Does Seattle's terrain change how a house sells?

Yes, because hills, water and earthquakes show up on the disclosure form every seller must fill out. Seattle sits between Puget Sound on the west and Lake Washington on the east, and the city is said to lie on seven hills. Capitol Hill, First Hill, Beacon Hill, Queen Anne, Magnolia and West Seattle are the usual list. The highest point inside the city limits is 520 feet above sea level at Myrtle Reservoir Park in High Point.

Seattle is in a major earthquake zone. The magnitude 6.8 Nisqually earthquake on February 28, 2001, caused heavy damage in Pioneer Square, which stands on reclaimed land, and the Seattle Fault runs just south of downtown. The climate is cool and wet in winter, with most of the year's rain falling between October and March, so roofs, basements and drainage get tested every year.

The state seller disclosure form asks about exactly these things. Among its questions are whether the roof has leaked in the last five years, whether the basement has flooded or leaked, whether there has been settling, slippage or sliding of the property, and whether any material damage came from earthquake, floods or landslides. A buyer's inspection will find the same issues you have to disclose.

What do I owe at closing when I sell in Seattle?

The largest line item for most sellers is Washington's real estate excise tax. The seller usually pays it, and if the seller does not, the buyer becomes responsible and an unpaid balance can become a lien on the property. The state portion is graduated, so each slice of the price is taxed at its own rate:

  • 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $525,000.
  • 1.28 percent on the part from $525,000 to $1,525,000.
  • 2.75 percent on the part from $1,525,000 to $3,025,000.
  • 3 percent on anything above $3,025,000.

The Department of Revenue shows new break points for sales beginning January 1, 2027: $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000, with the same four rates. As an illustration only, a sale at the $938,600 Census median value that closes before that date would carry roughly $11,069 of state tax ($5,775 on the first $525,000 plus $5,294 on the remaining $413,600). A local rate is added on top, and the Department of Revenue publishes a local rate table. Ask the King County treasurer or your closing agent which local rate applies to a Seattle address.

The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, which the state treats as the date the deed is notarized. If it is not paid within one month, interest runs on the unpaid amount, and the Department of Revenue lists a 6 percent rate for 2026 and 2027. Keep sale records for at least four years, since the state can audit a sale. Ask the King County treasurer for your parcel's property tax balance and due dates.

What paperwork does a Seattle seller have to hand over?

For an improved residential property, the seller must deliver a completed disclosure statement to the buyer unless the buyer has waived it or the transfer is exempt. Under RCW 64.06.020, delivery is due within five business days after both sides accept a written purchase contract, unless they agree otherwise.

The buyer then has three business days from delivery to rescind in writing, and the buyer may waive that right. The form is signed by the seller alone and is not a warranty. It covers title, water, sewer, structure, systems, homeowners' associations and environmental conditions, and it reminds the seller that carbon monoxide alarms and a smoke detection device must be in place.

Questions about work done on the house deserve extra care. The form asks whether there were conversions, additions or remodeling, and if so, whether all building permits and final inspections were obtained. If you finished a basement or added a bedroom years ago, pull your records before you answer.

I own a Seattle rental. What rules apply before I sell?

If tenants live in the house, two sets of rules apply: the city's rental registration program and the state's rules for ending a tenancy. Under the Rental Registration and Inspection Ordinance, rental housing must be registered with the city as soon as there is a tenant, and short-term rentals that are not the operator's primary residence must register before they are listed. A registration lasts two years. Fees and costs from the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections are below.

ItemAmount
Registration, one rental unit$126
Each additional unit at the same property$31.50
City inspector, one rental unit$241.50
City inspector, each additional unit$52.50
Filing fee for a private inspector's results$63
Penalty for a violation$150 a day for the first 10 days, then $500 a day

Source: Seattle SDCI, RRIO owners and managers. Properties are selected for an inspection once in the first five years, with a 10 percent chance of a second selection in the next five. A notice gives at least 60 days to finish the inspection, and tenants must get at least two days' notice of the visit. Missing smoke or carbon monoxide detectors, missing handrails and exposed wiring are among the common failures. The RRIO helpline is (206) 684-4110.

For a single-family house, RCW 59.18.650 lets an owner end a tenancy to sell with at least 90 days' advance written notice. The statute treats the owner as electing to sell only if the house is listed at a reasonable price within 30 days after the tenant leaves, and it presumes no intent to sell if the owner relists it as a rental or pulls it from the market within 90 days. A landlord who removes a tenant in violation of the section owes the greater of the tenant's damages or three times the monthly rent, plus attorney fees and court costs.

Which roads, schools and transit lines shape demand in Seattle?

Seattle Public Schools serves the vast majority of the city, and a small part of the Delridge neighborhood falls inside the Highline School District. Only Madison Street runs east to west without a break, and only Interstate 5 and State Route 99 run uninterrupted from north to south.

Rail has changed which addresses are convenient. Link light rail's 1 Line reached Northgate in October 2021 and Lynnwood in August 2024, and the 2 Line opened between Bellevue and Redmond in April 2024 and was extended to Seattle in March 2026. Regional voters approved Sound Transit 3 in November 2016, which calls for light rail to West Seattle and Ballard. The Alaskan Way Viaduct was replaced by a tunnel in 2019.

Amazon, Starbucks, Expeditors International of Washington, Nordstrom, Weyerhaeuser, Expedia Group and Zillow had their headquarters in Seattle on the Fortune 500's 2022 list, and the Port of Seattle is a major trade gateway.

When does a cash sale make sense for a Seattle house?

A cash sale fits a house that needs repairs, an inherited property, a rental with difficult tenants, or a seller who must move on a fixed date. Before you accept any offer, check these items:

  • Ask who pays the state and local excise tax and any title or escrow charges, and get the answer in writing.
  • Confirm the closing date and whether the buyer will accept the house with tenants in place.
  • Compare the offer with recent sales of similar homes near you.
  • Check your rental registration status with the RRIO program if the house has been rented.
  • Collect permits for any additions, since you still answer the permit question on the seller disclosure form.

You can request a cash offer for your Seattle house and compare it with a listing estimate before you decide. The excise tax and property tax items above apply either way.

More questions about Seattle, WA

Who pays the real estate excise tax when I sell a house in Seattle?

The seller usually pays it. If the seller does not, the buyer is responsible, and an unpaid amount can create a lien on the property. The tax goes to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the state rate is graduated from 1.1 percent up to 3 percent, with a local rate added.

Do I have to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Seattle?

Yes, in most sales of improved residential property. RCW 64.06.020 requires delivery within five business days after the contract is accepted, unless the buyer waived the statement or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days to rescind in writing.

Do I need to register my Seattle rental before I sell it?

If it has a tenant, it should be registered. Seattle requires registration as soon as there is a tenant in the rental space, and a registration lasts two years. Late registration or a missed inspection can bring penalties of $150 a day for the first 10 days and $500 a day after that.

Can I sell a Seattle house that has tenants in it?

Yes. A buyer can purchase it with the lease in place. If you want the tenant out so you can sell a single-family house, RCW 59.18.650 requires at least 90 days' written notice and a genuine attempt to list the house within 30 days after the tenant leaves.

What if my Seattle house has an addition built without a permit?

You can still sell it, but you must answer the permit question on the state disclosure form honestly. The form asks whether additions or remodeling were done and whether permits and final inspections were obtained. Ask the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections what records exist for your address.

What should a Spokane seller know about the local housing picture?

Spokane homeowners hold a median home value of $363,500, and 58.8 percent of households own the place they live, according to the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates. The city had an estimated 230,783 residents on July 1, 2025, up 0.8 percent from the April 2020 base.

Spokane sits on the Spokane River in eastern Washington at 1,843 feet above sea level, about 18 miles from the Idaho border and 229 miles east of Seattle. The city covers 60.02 square miles. A citywide median says little about one block, so compare against recent sales on your own street.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Spokane city, Washington.

How do the 2026 wildfires affect selling a house in Spokane?

They matter a great deal if your house or street was touched. In early August 2026 the Old Trails Fire destroyed more than 600 buildings, which the encyclopedia entry for Spokane calls the worst disaster in the city's history, and the City of Spokane has since run a recovery program for burned and damaged properties.

The city's wildfire information page and the county's recovery pages point owners to several resources:

  • Owners of properties hit by the Old Trails Fire can request an asbestos survey at no cost.
  • Residential applicants for rebuilding permits can use a free application completeness screening from Permavia for one year, which is optional and does not replace the city's own review.
  • The city issued its first rebuild permit after the fires on August 28, 2026.
  • Spokane County publishes a Demolition and Rebuilding FAQ and a Next Steps FAQ for affected owners.
  • Call 311 inside the city, or 509.755.CITY (2489) from outside it, Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.

Owners who lost a house or hold a damaged one often weigh rebuilding against selling the lot or the shell. Ask your insurer in writing what a sale does to an open claim before you sign anything, and ask the county assessor how the damage changes your assessed value.

Which Spokane neighborhoods and schools shape what a house is worth?

The answer starts with where the house sits. Downtown and the Riverside neighborhood form the business center, the South Hill rises south of it, and Browne's Addition west of downtown is a National Historic District known for Queen Anne and Craftsman mansions. Hillyard in the northeast began in 1892 as the site of the Great Northern Railway yard. East Central, the University District and West Central round out the older core, and the city counts 18 National Register historic districts. If your home is in one, ask the city's planning staff whether exterior changes need design review before you repaint, re-side or replace windows for a sale.

Most of the city falls within Spokane Public Schools (District 81), the largest public district in the city. The Mead School District serves parts of north Spokane County outside city limits. Gonzaga University, founded in 1887, and Whitworth University, which moved to north Spokane in 1914, are the two best-known campuses in the city.

Jobs follow the same pattern. Education, health care and social assistance employ 26.5 percent of working residents, retail trade 12.7 percent, and the 92d Air Refueling Wing at Fairchild Air Force Base near Airway Heights is the largest military employer. Weather also reaches the house: Spokane averages about 16.5 inches of precipitation a year, 21 days at or above 90 degrees and roughly 2.2 days at or below zero, so roofs, furnaces and insulation get tested at both ends.

What permit steps and city rules come up before a Spokane sale?

Any repair that needed a permit should be closed out with the city before you list. Spokane runs permits through its Accela Citizen Access portal, and the Development Services Center keeps in-person hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday and 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Wednesday. The center is closed on November 26 and 27 for the holiday.

  • Pull permit history for work you did or inherited, such as a finished basement, a new deck or a water heater swap.
  • Ask the permit center how to resolve an open or expired permit before a buyer's inspector finds it.
  • Pay only through the city's portal. The city warns that fake permit invoices are circulating and says it never asks for payment through emailed wire instructions.

The county's parcel information search shows tax history and assessed value for any Spokane parcel, which helps you confirm the lot size and legal description that will go on the deed.

What taxes and paperwork apply when a Spokane house sells?

The seller normally pays Washington's real estate excise tax, and it is due to the county treasurer where the property sits on the date of sale, whether or not the deed has been recorded yet. For Spokane that means the Spokane County Treasurer. The state share is graduated: 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the slice up to $1,525,000, with the thresholds rising to $551,000 and $1,551,000 for sales that start on January 1, 2027. A local share is added on top, so ask the treasurer for the exact combined rate before you set your net.

Tax not paid within one month of the sale collects interest, which the Department of Revenue lists at 6 percent for 2026. An unpaid tax can also become a lien on the property.

On most house sales you must hand the buyer a completed seller disclosure statement within five business days after both sides sign the purchase contract, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind unless the two of you agree otherwise (RCW 64.06.020). The form asks about structure, roof, systems, smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and the buyer may waive receiving it. Read the statute and the Department of Revenue's excise tax page before closing.

When does a cash sale make sense for a Spokane house?

A cash sale fits when speed or condition matters more to you than the last few thousand dollars. A listing usually asks for repairs, showings and a financing timeline. A cash buyer takes the house in the shape it is in and can often close on a date you choose, which helps with a fire-damaged home, an inherited house or a rental with a problem tenant.

Before you accept any offer from a Spokane buyer, get these points in writing:

  • The purchase price and who pays the excise tax and recording costs.
  • The closing date and the title or escrow company that will handle it.
  • Whether the buyer will take the house with its repairs, its contents and any open permits.
  • How long the offer stays open and what happens to any earnest money.

Compare that offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs. If the cash number is lower, the gap is the price of skipping the work and the wait.

How fast can I sell a house in Spokane?

The timeline depends on the route you pick. A cash purchase has no loan approval to wait for, so it can move faster than a listing, but title work and the escrow company set the real closing date.

Who pays the real estate excise tax on a Spokane sale?

The seller usually pays it. It is due to the Spokane County Treasurer on the date of sale, and the state portion is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price plus a local portion. Ask the treasurer for the combined rate.

Can I sell a fire-damaged house in Spokane?

Yes. Owners affected by the August 2026 Old Trails Fire can request a free asbestos survey from the city, and the county publishes demolition and rebuilding guidance. Talk to your insurer first about how a sale affects an open claim.

Do I have to give a Spokane buyer a seller disclosure statement?

Usually yes. Washington requires a completed form within five business days after the contract is signed on most residential sales, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

Where do I check property tax history for a Spokane house?

Use the Spokane County parcel information search, which lists tax history and assessed value. For a payoff or proration at closing, ask the Spokane County Treasurer.

What does the Tacoma housing market look like to a seller?

Tacoma homeowners report a median home value of $479,600 in the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates, and 55.8 percent of households own rather than rent. The city is the county seat of Pierce County and the economic center of the South Sound region, with an estimated 229,816 residents on July 1, 2025.

The median gross rent of $1,676 matters if you own a house that tenants occupy. Tacoma households earn a median of $85,884, and workers spend an average of 28.8 minutes getting to their jobs. Joint Base Lewis-McChord lies several miles south of the city, and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport is 22 miles north in SeaTac.

Which Tacoma neighborhoods do buyers ask about?

Buyers tend to ask which part of town a house is in before anything else. The city is grouped into Central Tacoma, New Tacoma around downtown, North Tacoma, Northeast Tacoma, West Tacoma and the Port of Tacoma area, and each carries its own character.

  • Central Tacoma includes Hilltop, Delong Park, the Wedge, Bryant and College Heights.
  • North Tacoma includes the Proctor District, the North Slope, Old Tacoma, Ruston Way, Skyline and Yakima Hill.
  • West Tacoma includes the Highlands, Narrows, Titlow and Salmon Beach.
  • Downtown takes in the Stadium District, the Theater District, the Dome District and the Thea Foss Waterway.

Transit shapes demand around the core. Sound Transit runs the T Line between Tacoma Dome Station, downtown, the University of Washington Tacoma campus and Hilltop, and also operates Sounder trains and express buses toward Seattle. Most of the city belongs to Tacoma Public Schools, which lists 36 elementary schools, 11 middle schools and 10 high schools, including Stadium High School and Mount Tahoma High School. Ruston is a separately incorporated town and Browns Point is unincorporated, so confirm which jurisdiction your parcel sits in before you ask the City of Tacoma about permits. Tacoma also keeps a historic preservation program with 165 city landmarks and more than 1,000 historic properties across five overlay zones, so ask the city whether your older home sits in one before you plan exterior work.

How do Tacoma's land, water and climate affect a house?

Elevation and shoreline do most of the work. The city ranges from sea level to roughly 500 feet and covers 62.34 square miles, of which 12.62 square miles are water, and it wraps around Commencement Bay on Puget Sound. Many parts of the city have views of Mount Rainier, and the low-lying ground near the Port of Tacoma sits in the path of a lahar from the Puyallup River if the volcano ever erupts.

Tacoma has a warm-summer Mediterranean climate, with July and August the warmest months and December the coldest. Mean daily highs run 48.1 degrees in January and 76.9 in August. The industrial tide flats once produced the odor known as the Tacoma Aroma, which ended when the Simpson Tacoma Kraft mill closed in September 2023.

The Port of Tacoma is among the largest seaports in the Pacific Northwest, and a refinery has operated on the tide flats since 1952. Downtown has been revitalized since the 1990s, with the University of Washington Tacoma campus, the T Line and a restored Thea Foss Waterway. The Tacoma Narrows bridges connect the city to Gig Harbor and the Kitsap Peninsula.

What property maintenance changes are coming for Tacoma owners?

Tacoma adopted a new property maintenance standard that takes effect on January 1, 2027. The City Council passed Ordinance 29125, which brings International Property Maintenance Code standards into the city's Property Maintenance and Nuisance Code and strengthens the tools the city uses against repeat and chronic violations.

The city says it handles roughly 4,500 property maintenance cases a year under older rules in Chapters 8.30 and 2.01 of its code. Section 7 of the ordinance states that the expanded enforcement program becomes operational no earlier than nine months after the council funds it, so the day-to-day effect depends on future budget decisions. If you own a vacant, neglected or rental house in Tacoma, find out whether any open code complaint is attached to it, and read the details at tacoma.gov/IPMC. Ask the city for any open complaint on the property before you list.

Pierce County bills and collects property tax for Tacoma addresses through the Assessor-Treasurer's office at 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, in Tacoma, reachable at (253) 798-6111. The second-half 2026 payment deadline was November 2, so a closing now should settle any unpaid balance and prorate the part of the year that the buyer will own. Payments can be made online through the parcel search site, by phone at (253) 798-3333, by mail to Pierce County Finance, or at the cashier lobby at 1501 Market St., Suite 120, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. Newer exemption rules also matter: starting in January 2027 more Pierce County homeowners who are 61 or older, or who have a qualifying disability, will see their taxes reduced under an expanded state program.

Real estate excise tax is due from the seller at the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state portion is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the amount between $525,000 and $1,525,000, and a local portion is added. Under RCW 64.06.020, a seller of most improved residential property must deliver a signed disclosure statement within five business days after the buyer and seller sign a contract. The form includes questions about the roof, plumbing, electrical and heating systems, and it notes that the seller must provide carbon monoxide alarms and at least one smoke detection device.

  • Gather your latest tax statement and any special assessments before listing.
  • Ask the county for the payoff amount on any unpaid taxes.
  • Collect permit records for additions, such as a converted garage or a new bathroom.
  • Check whether the city or the county has any open complaint or lien tied to the parcel.

Should I list my Tacoma house or take a cash offer?

The answer turns on your repair budget, your calendar and how much work the house needs before a buyer's inspector walks through. A listing exposes the house to the open market. A cash offer trades some of that exposure for speed and fewer conditions, which suits a vacant house, an inherited property or a rental with a tenant in place.

Whichever route you choose, compare written offers on net proceeds, not on the headline price. Ask each buyer who pays the excise tax, how long the offer is open, what the closing date is and whether they accept the house as it stands with its contents.

Can I sell a house in Tacoma that needs repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer may purchase the house as it stands, and on most residential sales you must complete the seller disclosure statement describing the property's condition to the best of your knowledge.

What does Ordinance 29125 mean for Tacoma sellers?

It sets a new property maintenance standard that takes effect January 1, 2027. The expanded enforcement program starts no earlier than nine months after the council funds it, so check for open code complaints on your property before you sell.

Who collects property tax on a Tacoma house?

Pierce County does, through its Assessor-Treasurer's office in Tacoma. Call (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and exemptions, and ask for a payoff figure before closing.

Who pays the excise tax when a Tacoma house sells?

The seller usually pays it, and it is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state rate is graduated, starting at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, with a local portion added.

The Census Bureau estimates 229,816 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 219,346 at the April 2020 census. Tacoma is the third most populous city in Washington.

How fast can I sell a house in Vancouver, WA?

The pace of a Vancouver sale depends on the buyer's money, the title work and one county step that every Clark County deed passes through. A buyer who pays cash removes the lender from the timeline, which is why owners facing a move, an inherited house or a repair bill often ask for cash offers. A traditional listing adds showings, an appraisal and a loan approval on top.

Vancouver is the seat of Clark County, on the north bank of the Columbia River directly across from Portland. The Census Bureau puts the population at 199,698 as of July 1, 2025, up 4.6 percent from the 2020 base. That growth means plenty of buyers and plenty of investors looking at the same streets you live on, so comparing more than one offer is realistic here.

What do the numbers say about the Vancouver housing market?

Census data gives a baseline for what a typical Vancouver home looks like on paper. The figures below come from the Census Bureau QuickFacts table for Vancouver city.

MeasureVancouver city
Residents (2025 estimate)199,698
Share of homes lived in by owners50.8%

Median monthly rent$1,702
Households81,504
Average commute23.2 minutes

With 50.8 percent of homes owner-occupied, about half of Vancouver housing is rented. A house that needs work can interest a landlord or investor as much as a buyer who plans to live in it.

Which parts of Vancouver have the oldest housing?

West Vancouver holds downtown and most of the older parts of the city, while East Vancouver grew after the 1997 annexation, which added 11,258 acres and 58,171 residents. NE Andresen Road is the usual dividing line between the two halves.

Several well-known neighborhoods began as wartime housing. When the Kaiser shipyard drew tens of thousands of workers in the 1940s, the Vancouver Housing Authority was created along with six residential developments: Fruit Valley, Fourth Plain Village, Bagley Downs, Ogden Meadows, Burton Homes and McLoughlin Heights. If your house is in one of those areas, expect a buyer's inspector to look closely at age-related items.

  • Original wiring and panels
  • Galvanized or older supply plumbing
  • Foundations, crawl spaces and drainage
  • Roofs and insulation

More than a third of the Vancouver urban area lives in unincorporated pockets such as Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek, which are outside city limits. Find out first whether your address is inside city limits, since the permit and rental rules below apply only there.

How do Vancouver's weather and river affect a house?

Vancouver has a warm-summer Mediterranean climate with about 42 inches of precipitation a year. Rain is frequent from fall through spring and tapers off around mid June, so roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take most of the wear. Cold east winds funnel down the Columbia River Gorge, and the city has seen freezing-rain storms that coat trees and power lines in ice.

The Columbia has flooded the area before, with destructive events in June 1894 and May 1948, though dams have since narrowed the river's swings. Tornadoes have also touched the metro area, including an EF1 that crossed from Vancouver Lake toward Hazel Dell on January 10, 2008. A buyer's inspector will look hardest at the roof, gutters and crawl space, so those are the places to check before you set a price.

What employers, schools and roads matter to Vancouver buyers?

Health care leads local employment. According to the city's 2022 financial report as summarized on Wikipedia, PeaceHealth is the largest employer with 16,500 employees, followed by Vancouver Public Schools, Evergreen Public Schools, The Vancouver Clinic and Battle Ground Public Schools.

Schools are a selling point in two main districts. Vancouver Public Schools covers most of west Vancouver, and Evergreen Public Schools covers most of the east side. Small portions of the city fall in the Camas and Battle Ground districts, so verify the district against your street address.

Commuting shapes demand. Interstates 5 and 205 both cross the Columbia into Portland, SR 14 runs east from downtown, and SR 500 links I-5 to I-205. Rush-hour traffic is heavy on the Interstate Bridge and the Glenn Jackson Bridge, and C-Tran runs local and express bus service. Homes near the freeways often draw commuters who value the shorter trip.

Do I need a permit before selling a Vancouver house?

You need one only if you plan to do the work yourself before closing. The City of Vancouver requires a residential building permit for the construction, alteration, addition, repair or demolition of residential buildings.

The city's residential permit page lists projects that need one:

  • Additions and remodels
  • Adding a garage, carport, deck or patio cover
  • Adding or removing walls
  • Converting a basement, attic or garage into living space
  • Changing the footprint of a structure

Small stand-alone electrical, mechanical or plumbing jobs fall under a trade permit instead. If you suspect past work was done without a permit, the city offers a field evaluation permit, where inspectors decide what permits and corrections are needed. Tree removal also needs a city permit. The Permit Center can be reached at 360-487-7833 for questions.

The city's updated zoning code took effect on July 31, 2026, and it allows more middle housing, up to six units on one lot. A buyer with development plans may value a lot differently than a buyer who wants to move in.

What changes if the Vancouver house is a rental?

Landlords selling in city limits should know about two programs. Since January 1, 2026, owners of residential rentals in Vancouver must register each unit every year, at $30 per unit. The free 90-day window closed on March 31, 2026. Health and safety inspections are planned to begin in mid 2027.

The city's rental registration page covers the sale of a registered rental: the registration must be transferred to the new owner within 60 days of the property transfer, with no extra fee. If you stop renting, you can deregister the property. Questions go to rentalregistration@cityofvancouver.us or 360-487-7928.

Short-term rentals are a separate permit. Vancouver defines one as a rental of fewer than 30 consecutive nights, and the permit requires a Washington business license with the city endorsement, at least $1 million in liability insurance and a notice mailed to abutting neighbors. The city caps total permits at 870, or about 1 percent of its housing stock. A permit does not override a lease or homeowners association rules, so a buyer who plans to use the house this way should confirm the status with the city's short-term rental page.

How do the deed and excise tax work in Clark County?

Every Clark County sale runs through the Treasurer first and the Auditor second. The Treasurer collects the real estate excise tax, and RCW 82.45.090 bars the Auditor from taking a deed for recording until the tax is paid or the Treasurer marks it not due.

The Clark County Treasurer states that the tax is due 30 days from the date of sale and that a $5 processing fee is added. The state part is graduated by sale price:

  • 1.10 percent on a price up to $525,000
  • 1.28 percent from $525,000.01 to $1,525,000
  • 2.75 percent from $1,525,000.01 to $3,025,000
  • 3.00 percent above $3,025,000

A local rate is added on top, so ask the Treasurer or your closing agent for the total on your price. In person, the office is at 1300 Franklin Street, 2nd Floor, Monday to Thursday from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. After payment, the Auditor's Recording Department at the same address records the deed. Its recording guide lists 564-397-2208 for questions.

A third piece of paperwork is the seller disclosure. RCW 64.06.020 sets out the form for improved residential property, and the seller hands it over no later than five business days after a written purchase contract is mutually accepted, unless the parties choose another schedule. A buyer who receives it has a three-business-day window to rescind.

More questions about Vancouver, WA

Can I sell a Vancouver, WA house as-is?

Yes, as-is sales are common. The state's seller disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 still applies to improved residential property, and unpermitted work you know of belongs on it.

Who records the deed when a Vancouver house sells?

The Clark County Auditor's Recording Department records it, but only after the Treasurer's Office handles the excise tax affidavit. Both offices are at 1300 Franklin Street, and title or escrow companies normally submit the paperwork for you.

What happens to my Vancouver rental registration when I sell?

It transfers to the new owner. The city says the registration must be moved within 60 days of the property transfer, and there is no additional fee. If the buyer will live in the home, the registration can be ended through deregistration.

Does Vancouver cap short-term rental permits?

Yes. The city limits permits to 870, or about 1 percent of its total housing stock. Anyone buying a house to run as a short-term rental should check permit availability with the Permit Center before paying a premium for that use.

Which school district is my Vancouver house in?

Most of west Vancouver is in Vancouver Public Schools and most of east Vancouver is in Evergreen Public Schools. Small portions are in the Camas and Battle Ground districts, so check the address with the district before you describe it to a buyer.

What is it like to sell a house in Bellevue, WA?

Bellevue is a high-value market: the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $1,340,300 for 2020 to 2024, and estimates 154,193 residents as of July 1, 2025. About 52.0% of housing is owner-occupied, median household income is $165,576, and median gross rent is $2,572.

The population is diverse and highly educated: 43.5% of residents were born outside the United States, 48.8% of those age five and older speak a language other than English at home, and 72.1% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The average commute is 23.6 minutes. The city covers 37.5 square miles of land and water combined and had 151,854 residents at the 2020 census, up from 122,363 in 2010.

Where is Bellevue, and how did it grow?

Bellevue is an Eastside city in King County, across Lake Washington from Seattle and between that lake and Lake Sammamish. Interstate 405 runs through it north to south, Interstate 90 crosses the southern part, and State Route 520 roughly marks the northern edge. Kirkland and Redmond sit to the north, Issaquah to the east, Mercer Island across the East Channel Bridge, and Newcastle and Renton to the south. South of I-90 the city climbs Cougar Mountain.

William Meydenbauer and Aaron Mercer claimed homesteads here in 1869, and permanent residents arrived around 1879. Logging came first, and Japanese immigrant labor later cleared much of the land for small farms. The Bellevue Strawberry Festival began in 1925. The Lake Washington Floating Bridge opened in 1940 and the Evergreen Point Floating Bridge in 1963, and the second bridge set off faster growth. Bellevue incorporated on March 31, 1953, annexed Crossroads in 1964 and Lake Hills in 1969, and by the 1970 census was the fourth most populous city in the state.

Which neighborhoods and school districts matter to Bellevue buyers?

The city names fourteen neighborhoods, and the list below groups them for easier reading.

  • Downtown, Wilburton/BelRed and Eastgate/Factoria.
  • Bridle Trails, Northwest Bellevue, Northeast Bellevue and West Bellevue.
  • Crossroads, Lake Hills, Newport and Somerset.
  • Cougar Mountain/Lakemont, Woodridge and West Lake Sammamish.

The vast majority of the city is served by the Bellevue School District, whose main public high schools are Bellevue High, Interlake, Newport and Sammamish, with International School and Big Picture School as choice programs. Portions of the city lie in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah school districts, so check the district for your address. Bellevue College is in the city, as are several independent schools such as Bellevue Christian School and Open Window School.

How do jobs and light rail affect Bellevue home values?

Employment is the engine. According to the city's 2024 financial report, Amazon is the largest employer with 14,300 workers, followed by T-Mobile (7,800), Meta (5,400), Overlake Hospital Medical Center (3,800) and the Bellevue School District (2,900). Downtown Bellevue is the second largest city center in Washington, with about 1,300 businesses, 45,000 employees and 10,200 residents.

Transit has caught up with the jobs. Sound Transit's 2 Line runs from Lynnwood to Redmond through Seattle, Mercer Island and Bellevue. The first section, South Bellevue to Redmond Technology station, opened April 27, 2024, and the Seattle to Bellevue section opened in March 2026. The Bellevue Transit Center downtown serves both King County Metro and Sound Transit buses, and a fare-free electric shuttle run by Circuit began operating in August 2023.

The weather is typical Puget Sound. Bellevue averages about 32 inches of rain a year, with frequent showers from October to May, though 2016 reached 47.14 inches. Highs in July and August average in the high 70s.

Can a Bellevue house be rented short term?

Usually not as a whole house. Bellevue's Land Use Code defines transient lodging as a stay of less than 30 days, and an entire single-family home or a home with an accessory dwelling unit cannot be used that way. Long-term rentals of 30 days or more are allowed, and an ADU may be rented only on a long-term basis. This matters if a buyer is counting on vacation-rental income, so state the limits clearly when you list.

Type of homeShort-term rental rule
Entire single-family home, or home with an ADUNot allowed for transient lodging.
Rooms in an owner-occupied single-family homeAllowed as a boarding house or bed and breakfast: owner-occupied, at most two rooms and two adults per room, with an approved home occupation permit (LUC 20.20.140).
Apartment, condo or planned unit development in a residential districtAllowed with a Short-Term Stay Use Registration Notice, limited to five units and 20% of the units in the development (LUC 20.20.800).

Source: City of Bellevue Residential Rental Regulations. Development Services Land Use answers questions at 425-452-4188 or landusereview@bellevuewa.gov.

Which work on a Bellevue house needs a permit?

Many common projects do. Bellevue Development Services publishes a list of work that requires permits, and these are the examples most likely to come up before a sale.

  • Additions that add square footage, including a second story or dormers, need a permit with plan review.
  • Converting a garage or carport into living space needs a permit with plan review.
  • Decks with a walking surface more than 30 inches above the ground need a permit with plan review.
  • Interior remodels that create new walls or turn a basement into living area need a permit.
  • Furnaces, heat pumps, new gas lines, new electrical circuits and EV charging stations need permits.
  • An interior accessory dwelling unit needs approval, and the review takes several weeks.

Some work needs nothing. The city does not require a permit for replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops, replacing a window or door with the same size in the same spot, or building a fence under eight feet tall, though fences over 4.5 feet often cannot sit in front-yard setbacks. Emergency repairs such as a failed water heater or furnace can start first, with the permit obtained on the first city work day afterward.

How are taxes and closing handled when selling in Bellevue?

King County bills property tax on a Bellevue house. Under RCW 84.56.020 the first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31, and RCW 84.60.020 makes the tax a lien from January 1 and divides the year between seller and buyer by days when the contract is silent. Your escrow officer normally prorates the bill at closing and pays any unpaid amount from your proceeds.

Washington law also requires a seller disclosure statement for improved residential property. Under RCW 64.06.020 you must deliver it within five business days after a written contract is mutually accepted unless the buyer waived it, and the buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.

The state real estate excise tax is usually paid by the seller and is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the rates are 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3% above. At Bellevue's census median value of $1,340,300 the state share would be about $16,164 before the local portion, which your closing agent can confirm.

Can I rent my whole Bellevue house on a short-term basis?

No. Bellevue does not allow an entire single-family home or a home with an ADU to be used for transient lodging, which is a stay under 30 days. Long-term rentals of 30 days or more are allowed.

Does replacing kitchen cabinets in Bellevue need a permit?

A building permit is not required for replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops. A plumbing or electrical permit may still be needed if that work is part of the job.

Which school district serves my Bellevue home?

Most of the city is in the Bellevue School District, but portions are in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah districts. Check the district for your exact address.

How soon must a Bellevue seller give the buyer the disclosure statement?

Within five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind.

How much state excise tax would a $1,340,300 Bellevue sale owe?

Under the rates for sales beginning January 1, 2027, the state portion would be about $16,164: 1.1% on the first $551,000 and 1.28% on the rest. A local portion is added.

What are my choices when I want to sell a house in Kent?

A Kent owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a purchase offer from a buyer who does not need a mortgage. Each path trades time, effort and price differently, so line them up against your own deadline before you decide.

  • Listing with an agent: Expect to stage, clean and repair, then wait through showings and a buyer's inspection and loan approval.
  • Selling on your own: You keep control of price and terms and take on the marketing, the contract and the closing paperwork yourself.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: The sale moves without lender underwriting. Ask for the net amount you would receive at closing and compare it with the other two routes.

A building with tenants raises extra questions, covered below, because Kent runs its own rental inspection program.

How is Kent laid out, and where does flooding come up?

Kent is divided into three sections: West Hill, along Interstate 5; the Valley, mostly industrial and commercial with some medium-density housing and parkland along the Green River; and East Hill, which is largely residential with retail. Downtown Kent sits on the east side of the valley, about 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. Renton, Covington, Auburn, Federal Way, Des Moines, SeaTac and Tukwila all touch the city. The city covers 34.167 square miles, and Lake Meridian on East Hill is its largest lake, with Clark Lake and Lake Fenwick surrounded by city parks.

The Green River matters to anyone selling in the Valley. Wikipedia notes that flooding from the Green and White rivers was a constant problem in the early 1900s, and that the river kept causing trouble until Howard A. Hanson Dam went up at Eagle Gorge in 1962. The City of Kent maintains a Floodplains page with flood resources and FEMA elevation certificates, plus a Green River flooding information page. If your house is near the river, ask the city for the elevation certificate and floodplain status before a buyer asks.

What shaped Kent's economy and population?

Kent was incorporated on May 28, 1890, the second city in King County after Seattle. Its early money came from hops, and the town took its name in 1889 from the English hop county; later came dairy, then a stretch as the lettuce capital of the world. After World War II the city grew quickly, twelvefold between 1953 and 1960, and Boeing began building in Kent in 1965.

Today the Valley is a warehouse and manufacturing district. Wikipedia says manufacturing and distribution in Kent and the surrounding area ranks fourth among markets in the United States. Blue Origin and Stoke Space have their headquarters here, and Amazon, Boeing, Whirlpool and General Electric run large facilities. On July 1, 2010 the city annexed the Panther Lake area, adding about 5 square miles and 24,000 residents.

Does Kent regulate rental housing, and does that touch my sale?

Yes, for buildings with two or more units. The City Council passed an ordinance in 2018 requiring periodic health and safety inspections by a qualified inspector for apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes inside city limits. A standalone house is not on that list. If you own a duplex or a small building and plan to sell, the program shapes what a buyer will ask about.

  • Registration: Covered rentals are registered online every year, with a deadline of November 1. The 2026 date has passed, and the next is November 1, 2027.
  • Inspection cycle: Each property is inspected once every three years. North East Hill, north of James Street, is on the 2026 cycle; West Hill and the Valley, west of Highway 167, are due in 2027; South East Hill, south of James Street, in 2028.
  • Penalties: Owners whose units fail must make repairs and pass reinspection before renewing the multi-family business license. Failure can bring penalty fees and revocation of the license.

For license questions, the city lists 253-856-5200. Ask the city which cycle year your address falls in before you set a closing date, and keep the latest inspection paperwork with your sale file.

What do I file and pay at closing on a Kent sale?

The big item is the state real estate excise tax. According to the Department of Revenue, the seller usually pays it, and if the seller does not, the buyer is responsible. State tax is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the next slice up to $1,525,000, with a local rate added. A Kent sale at the $587,800 median home value would carry about $6,579 in state tax, made up of $5,775 and about $804.

A transfer by deed needs an excise tax affidavit, the deed and payment. The department warns that mailing the affidavit and deed to the Department of Revenue by mistake can delay the filing with the county and lead to penalties and interest. Take them to the county treasurer where the property sits, which for Kent is King County, or let your escrow officer handle the filing. Payment is due on the date of sale, and penalty and interest apply if it is not paid within one month.

Which permits does Kent ask about on a house sale?

Kent's Permit Center takes electronic applications by appointment and issues residential permits for additions and alterations, plumbing, re-roofing and mechanical work. The city publishes separate short forms for a residential plumbing permit, which covers replacing fixtures and hot water tanks, for a re-roof, and for mechanical equipment including gas piping. If a previous owner swapped a water heater or replaced a roof, ask the Permit Center whether a permit was pulled, and check the Permit Logs page for issued permits.

Code Enforcement is the city office tasked with keeping Kent safe and beautiful, so ask it whether any case is open on your property before you set a closing date.

How do roads, transit and schools affect Kent buyers?

State Route 167 runs north to Renton and south to Puyallup, and the city also includes parts of Interstate 5 and State Route 18, with State Route 516 crossing east to west. Kent Station is the hub for Sounder commuter trains to Seattle and Tacoma, plus King County Metro and Sound Transit Express buses, and RapidRide A runs along SR 99 in west Kent. The I Line is scheduled to connect downtown Kent with Renton and Auburn in 2027. Average travel time to work is 30.4 minutes.

The Kent School District covers most of the city, with four high schools, seven middle schools, 28 elementary schools and two academies. Parts of Kent fall in Federal Way Public Schools, Tahoma, Highline or the Renton School District, so confirm the district for your address when you write a listing or describe the house to a buyer.

More questions about Kent, WA

Does Kent's rental inspection program cover a single-family house?

No. The program's list is apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes, each with two or more units. Owners of those buildings register every year by November 1 and have an inspection once every three years.

Where do I file the excise tax affidavit for a Kent sale?

With the county treasurer in the county where the property is located, which is King County for Kent. The Department of Revenue says to submit the affidavit, the deed and the payment there, and warns that sending them to the department by mistake can cause delays.

Which school district serves my Kent address?

Most of Kent is in the Kent School District. Portions are in Federal Way Public Schools, the Tahoma School District, Highline Public Schools or the Renton School District, with far east Kent zoned to Tahoma, so check the district for your specific address.

How far is Kent from Seattle?

Downtown Kent is about 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. State Route 167 and Interstate 5 are the main roads, and Sounder trains run from Kent Station to downtown Seattle during peak weekday hours.

Is flood risk a concern for Kent houses?

It can be in the Green River Valley. Howard A. Hanson Dam went up in 1962 after decades of flooding, and the city keeps a Floodplains page with FEMA elevation certificates. Ask the city about floodplain status for your parcel.

What should I know before selling a house in Everett, WA?

Everett is the Snohomish County seat, and a sale here runs through county offices for excise tax and property tax, plus the city for any permit questions. The city sits about 25 miles north of Seattle on the Port Gardner Peninsula, where the Snohomish River meets Possession Sound. The Census Bureau estimates 113,567 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 110,629 at the 2020 census.

Everett is a renter-heavy market. Only 49.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so a good share of sellers are landlords, heirs who inherited a rental, or owners of a house with a basement or backyard unit. That mix shapes which sale route fits: a vacant inherited house, a tenant-occupied duplex and a move-in-ready home on Rucker Hill each call for a different plan.

Everett's economy and layout explain much of the buyer demand. Boeing built its assembly plant at Paine Field in 1967, and Naval Station Everett has operated since 1994. Interstate 5 runs through the city, with US 2 heading to Stevens Pass and State Routes 526, 527 and 529 connecting neighborhoods. Everett Station serves Sounder commuter trains, Amtrak and buses, which matters to anyone commuting to Seattle.

What do Everett housing numbers look like?

Owner-occupied homes in Everett have a median value of $565,300, and 49.0 percent of housing is owner-occupied, per Census Bureau QuickFacts. Values marked 2020-2024 come from the five-year American Community Survey.

A median value of $565,300 describes owner-occupied homes citywide, not your house. Condition, lot and street all move the number, so treat it as a rough backdrop.

Which Everett neighborhoods and local conditions affect a sale?

Everett has 19 recognized neighborhood associations, and buyers shop by area. A few that come up often:

  • Bayside and Port Gardner: downtown, the waterfront and the historic Rucker Hill residential area.
  • Northwest Everett and Riverside: older homes near Everett Community College, with historic districts in both.
  • Lowell: southeast of downtown and once its own town, founded in 1863.
  • Silver Lake, Cascade View and Twin Creeks: south Everett, near Everett Mall and the lake.
  • Westmont: a mostly multifamily area in the southwest.

Most of the city belongs to Everett Public Schools. The southern and western neighborhoods are in the Mukilteo School District, so confirm the district for the address before you describe schools in a listing.

The southwestern neighborhoods include creek ravines that drain to Port Gardner Bay, and the area is prone to mudslides. The city averages about 35.71 inches of rain a year, mostly from October through March. If your lot sits on a slope or near a ravine, collect drainage and retaining wall records before buyers ask.

Can I sell an Everett house that has an accessory dwelling unit?

Yes, and Everett has loosened its rules. Under the city's ADU page, accessory dwelling units are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, and an ADU is defined as a unit under 1,000 square feet that is subordinate to the main home. The city allows up to two ADUs on a lot. Dwellings under 1,200 square feet need no off-street car parking.

Fee treatment matters to the next owner: transportation impact fees are waived for one added ADU, school impact fees are waived for ADUs, and park impact fees are cut by half. In June 2026 the city also launched a gallery of pre-approved ADU designs, with a licensing fee of about $1,500.

  • If the unit was built without a permit, ask Everett Permit Services at PermitServices@everettwa.gov what is needed to legalize it before you list.
  • The city counts basements and attics as ADU space, though not garages, and each separate dwelling unit needs its own utilities.
  • In a historic overlay, any ADU that is not entirely inside the existing home goes to the Historical Commission.

What are my choices if I need to sell fast in Everett?

Everett sellers usually pick among three routes, and the right one depends on the house and the deadline.

  • List with an agent: the widest buyer pool, with showings, inspections and financing contingencies that add weeks.
  • Sell directly to an investor or cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can often choose, usually at a price below a fully prepared listing.
  • Sell it yourself: saves a listing commission, but you handle disclosure forms, pricing and negotiation.

Whichever route you take, ask for the buyer's proof of funds, read the purchase agreement before signing and compare any offer to what you would net after taxes, liens and any loan payoff. A written offer from an escrow company's closing officer shows the figures line by line.

What taxes and paperwork apply when an Everett house sells?

Washington charges a real estate excise tax on each sale, and the Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays it. The state portion is graduated under RCW 82.45.060: 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 of the price, 1.28 percent on the portion up to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent up to $3,025,000 and 3 percent above that. For sales beginning January 1, 2027 the first tier ends at $551,000. A local rate is added on top, so get the combined figure from the Snohomish County Treasurer or your escrow officer.

For a deeded transfer, the excise tax affidavit, the conveyance document and payment go to the county treasurer. The Snohomish County Treasurer lists an excise tax counter open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and the office address is 3000 Rockefeller, Everett, WA 98201.

On the property tax side, Snohomish County bills in two halves: April 30 and October 31. Mail payments must be postmarked by the due date. The October 31, 2026 deadline has passed, so any unpaid second-half amount now carries interest and has to be cleared at closing. The next first-half deadline is April 30, 2027.

What happens if I am behind on Everett property taxes?

Late payments carry interest. Under RCW 84.56.020, residential property with four or fewer units is charged 9 percent a year on delinquent taxes, with no added penalties, while larger or nonresidential property faces 12 percent plus penalties. Snohomish County assesses the charge on the first day of each month, and missing the April 30 first-half payment makes the full year's tax delinquent.

The county also warns that a property can go to foreclosure once the third delinquent year's taxes are owed in full. Its Tax Lien Foreclosure Sale is run online, with the list of properties filed in court each May. If you are close to that point, a sale can pay the back taxes out of the proceeds at closing. The Treasurer's page also points to a statute that allows interest and penalties to be waived in limited situations, so ask the office whether you qualify.

How many people live in Everett, WA?

The Census Bureau estimates 113,567 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 110,629. Everett is the most populous city in Snohomish County.

Who pays the real estate excise tax when an Everett house sells?

The seller usually pays, according to the Washington Department of Revenue. If the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property. The state tiers are in RCW 82.45.060, and a local rate is added.

Are accessory dwelling units allowed in Everett?

Yes. ADUs are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, with up to two per lot and a size cap of 1,000 square feet under the city's definition. Check the permit history of any existing unit before you sell.

When are Snohomish County property taxes due?

First-half or full payment is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date. The October 31, 2026 date has already passed.

Which school district serves my Everett house?

Most of Everett is in Everett Public Schools, while the southern and western neighborhoods are served by the Mukilteo School District. Confirm the district for your exact address with the district or the county before you advertise schools.

What should I know before selling a house in Spokane Valley?

Spokane Valley is the largest suburb of Spokane and was the ninth-most populous city in Washington at the 2020 census. The Census Bureau estimates 108,405 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 5.2 percent from the 2020 base. The city covers 37.72 square miles of land along the Spokane River, east of Spokane and west of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, and it surrounds the separate city of Millwood on three sides. Locals call it "The Valley."

This table sets the city beside Seattle using Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024, so you can see how different the two markets are.

How did Spokane Valley become a city?

It became a city in 2003 by combining several unincorporated communities, and that history explains the mix of housing you see today. The Valley was farm and orchard country first, irrigated beginning in 1895. In 1940 about 10,000 people lived there, by 1960 roughly 45,000, and by 1970 the suburb held 60,000.

Voters approved incorporation on May 21, 2002, after four failed attempts. The City of Spokane Valley was incorporated on March 31, 2003, combining Dishman, Opportunity, Trentwood, Veradale, part of Greenacres and East Spokane, with Yardley and Chester also inside the boundaries. At that point it was the third-largest newly incorporated city in United States history. Supporters wanted a stronger local voice and feared annexation by Spokane, while opponents pointed to the risk of higher taxes.

Because the city grew in stages, its streets include many curved and discontinuous roads and cul-de-sacs, typical of postwar suburbs. The city sits at 2,038 feet. Precipitation averages just over 16 inches a year, July is the warmest month at an average of 73 degrees, and January averages 28.3 degrees.

Which roads and transit routes serve Spokane Valley?

Interstate 90 is the backbone, and the city is reached from exits 285 through 293. Commutes are short by regional standards, averaging 20.8 minutes. These are the corridors buyers mention most:

  • Sprague Avenue, the main retail corridor, also carries the Interstate 90 Business designation.
  • Trent Avenue is State Route 290 and runs northeast to the Idaho border.
  • Pines Road is the northern end of State Route 27, part of the Palouse Scenic Byway.
  • North to south arterials include Argonne and Mullan roads, Pines, Evergreen and Sullivan.
  • Spokane Transit Authority serves the city through the Pence-Cole Valley Transit Center, with a few park-and-ride locations.

Spokane International Airport is about 16 miles west in Spokane, and Felts Field, a general aviation airport, is on the city's northern edge. The state transportation department began installing ramp meters on Interstate 90 in 2019 to ease peak congestion, and the state reports increasing congestion at peak commute hours.

Which school districts cover Spokane Valley?

Several districts share the city. The Central Valley School District is the largest, with 14,593 students in preschool through twelfth grade, followed by the East Valley School District with 4,277 and the West Valley School District with 3,862. A portion of western Spokane Valley falls within Spokane Public Schools. Boundaries do not follow city limits, so confirm the district for your address before you describe the schools in a listing.

Private options include Valley Christian School and The Oaks Academy. Juniors and seniors can attend Spokane Valley Tech, a skills center supported by area districts, and Carrington College has a campus in the city. Residents also have a Spokane County Library District branch inside city limits. Adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher at a rate of 26.5 percent.

What does the city require for permits and business licenses?

The city requires a permit for new homes, duplexes, garages, decks, pools, spas and fences, and for any addition or interior alteration to a home. That last point matters if you changed the interior yourself. The Permit Center is at City Hall, 10210 E. Sprague Avenue, and the phone number is 509-720-5240. Applicants submit site plans and construction plans, along with a copy of the sewer permit, which Spokane County Utilities issues. Applications can be filed through the online portal, and paid by credit card (with a 2.5 percent convenience fee) or by check.

Spokane Valley requires every business to hold a state business license that is renewed each year, and the city's general license fee is $25 to start and $25 to renew. A home business needs its own permit. If you rent out the house, ask the city's Business Licensing Specialist at 509-720-5333 whether a rental needs a license or registration.

If you plan to sell a single-family rental with a tenant in it, RCW 59.18.650 requires at least 90 days' written notice, and the owner must list the house within 30 days after the tenant leaves.

What taxes and recording steps apply when I sell?

You pay through the Spokane County Treasurer, and the sequence matters. Washington's real estate excise tax applies to nearly every sale, and the county requires a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit and the deed to go to the Treasurer's office before the deed is presented to the Spokane County Auditor for recording. The county takes cash or a check payable to the Spokane County Treasurer and asks you not to mail cash. The Treasurer's number is 509-477-4713.

The state portion is 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $525,000, and higher rates apply above that. At the $382,300 Census median value, the state tax would be about $4,205, which is below the first break point. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, that break point rises to $551,000. A local rate is added on top, so ask the Treasurer or your closing agent for the figure. The seller usually pays, and the state treats the date the deed is notarized as the date of sale. Interest runs if payment is not made within one month.

Property tax runs on a separate schedule. Spokane County bills once a year with two payment coupons:

  • The first half is due April 30 and the second half is due October 31.
  • If the tax is under $50, the full amount is due April 30.
  • When a due date falls on a weekend or county holiday, the county accepts payment the next business day.
  • Both 2026 dates have passed, so the next one is April 30, 2027.
  • If no statement arrives by March 31, look it up on the county's SCOUT system or call the Treasurer.

You will also give the buyer the state seller disclosure statement within five business days after contract acceptance, and the buyer has three business days to rescind unless that right is waived. If the house needs repairs you would rather not make, you can request a cash offer for your Spokane Valley house and compare it with a listed sale.

The Census Bureau estimates 108,405 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 102,976, and the city incorporated on March 31, 2003.

When are Spokane County property taxes due?

The first half is due April 30 and the second half is due October 31. If the bill is under $50, the whole amount is due April 30. A due date that lands on a weekend or county holiday moves to the next business day.

How do I pay the real estate excise tax on a Spokane Valley sale?

Take the excise tax affidavit and the deed to the Spokane County Treasurer's office before the deed goes to the Auditor for recording. Payment is by cash or a check payable to the Spokane County Treasurer. Do not mail cash.

Do I need a permit to remodel before selling in Spokane Valley?

Yes, the city lists any interior alteration to a home, duplex or accessory structure as work that needs a residential permit. Additions, decks, pools, spas and fences also need one. Contact the Permit Center at 509-720-5240.

Which school district is my Spokane Valley house in?

It depends on the address. Central Valley, East Valley and West Valley serve most of the city, and part of the western edge is in Spokane Public Schools. Check the district's boundary map before you put a school name in a listing.

What are my options if I want to sell my house fast in Renton, WA?

Renton homeowners can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer and close on their own schedule. Speed, price and effort pull in different directions, so it helps to rank what you need before you talk to anyone.

Renton's housing stock is mixed. The Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $672,600 for 2020 to 2024, and just over half of households (54.4 percent) own the place they live in. That leaves a large renter population, which means many Renton sellers are landlords, heirs of a rental, or owners of a house with a basement or backyard unit. If that describes you, read the rental registration section further down before you set a closing date.

  • Choose a listing if the house is in good shape and you can wait through showings and buyer financing.
  • Choose a cash sale if repairs, tenants, an inherited property or a tight deadline make a traditional listing hard.
  • Choose a sale by owner only if you are comfortable handling the contract, the disclosure form and the excise tax affidavit.

Whatever you pick, compare offers on the same terms: price, closing date, who pays closing costs, and what happens if the buyer finds problems.

What is Renton like, and why does it matter to a seller?

Renton is an inner suburb of Seattle about 11 miles southeast of downtown, set on the southeast shore of Lake Washington at the mouth of the Cedar River. The city covers 25.27 square miles, borders Newcastle to the north and Kent to the south, and shares its western edge with Tukwila and the unincorporated West Hill area. King County's urban growth boundary runs along the east side, so no incorporated city sits directly east of it.

Settlers of European descent arrived in the 1850s and 1860s, and Erasmus Smithers is credited with founding the town in 1875 around coal, clay and timber. Renton incorporated on September 6, 1901. The Cedar and Black rivers flooded the town regularly until the Lake Washington Ship Canal opened in 1916, lowered the lake and led to the Cedar being diverted into the lake. That flood history is a good reason to check any property near the river against current floodplain maps.

The Boeing Renton Factory, opened in World War II to build the B-29, is the city's best known employer and still assembles the 737. The city grew from 4,488 residents in 1940 to 16,039 in 1950. Paccar's Kenworth truck plant, Providence Health and Wizards of the Coast also have a large presence. Renton sits where I-5, I-405 and SR 167 meet, which is why the area draws regional shoppers, an IKEA store that opened in 1994 and the Seattle Seahawks training facility.

Which Renton neighborhoods, schools and roads shape buyer interest?

Buyers sort Renton by commute, school district and distance to the lake or downtown. Downtown Renton has been redeveloped since the 1990s around a transit center and Piazza Park, which hosts a weekly farmers market. The Landing, a 68-acre residential and commercial development on former Boeing land near the south shore of Lake Washington, and the Southport lakefront development with its 347-room Hyatt Regency, round out the redeveloped waterfront.

Most of the city belongs to the Renton School District, which operates Hazen, Lindbergh, Renton and Albert Talley high schools. Smaller parts of Renton fall in the Issaquah, Kent and Tahoma districts, so confirm the district for your address before you advertise it. The areas of Fairwood, the East Renton Plateau and West Hill are unincorporated and are not part of the city, which matters if a buyer assumes city services and permits apply to them.

For commuters, King County Metro runs the RapidRide F Line through Renton. Sound Transit's Stride bus rapid transit is planned for 2028, and a new transit center for it south of downtown began construction in 2026. Renton's mean travel time to work was 29.7 minutes in the 2020 to 2024 Census data, longer than the 22.1 minutes reported for Redmond.

How do Renton's numbers look?

The estimate for 2025 is 1.8 percent below the April 2020 estimates base, so the city has not grown since the last census. Buyers in this market weigh price against commute, which is why a house within reach of the transit center or the freeway interchanges tends to draw more interest than one with a long drive to either.

Do Renton's rental registration and ADU rules affect my sale?

They can, if the house has a tenant or an accessory unit. Renton requires landlords and property managers to register residential rental properties every year on or before January 1. The program covers renter-occupied single family homes, condos, duplexes and apartment complexes, plus owner-occupied duplexes and homes that rent out an accessory dwelling unit. Registration is currently free. Short-term rentals and single room rentals need a City of Renton business license instead of registration.

The program enforces the state Landlord-Tenant Act and the city's building standards. When a violation is verified, the landlord has 15 days to respond and correct it. If you are selling a rental, close out any open warning first, because a buyer's inspector will find it.

Accessory units are also easier to build than before. Renton adopted Ordinance 6160 on June 16, 2025 to comply with state House Bill 1337, and the city's Permit Ready ADU program offers eight pre-approved plans at no charge to owners inside city limits. If your lot has room, a buyer who wants an ADU may value that option, and you can mention it in the listing. Check the city's current ADU rules before you promise anything specific.

What will the excise tax cost on a Renton sale?

The seller usually pays Washington's real estate excise tax, due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue treats as the date the deed is notarized. For sales beginning January 1, 2027 the state rate is 1.1 percent on the first $551,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the next slice up to $1,551,000.

As an illustration only, take a sale at the Census median value of $672,600. The first $551,000 at 1.1 percent is $6,061, and the remaining $121,600 at 1.28 percent is $1,556.48, for a state portion of $7,617.48. A local rate is added on top. Ask your escrow officer or the King County Recorder's Office for the local rate that applies to a Renton address and the brackets that apply if you close before the new year.

Keep records that support the price and any exemption you claim. The Department of Revenue says to retain them for at least four years, and a refund request must be filed within four years of the sale.

What disclosure and property tax steps should I plan for?

For most improved residential sales you must give the buyer a seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020 within five business days after the contract is accepted, unless the buyer waived it. The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind. The form asks about roof leaks in the last five years, flooding or drainage problems, shorelines, wetlands and floodplains, sewer connection, and whether building permits were obtained for any remodeling.

Property tax follows the parcel, so the closing agent should prorate it. Under RCW 84.56.020, the first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31 for bills of $50 or more. A late first-half payment starts interest, and for homes with four or fewer units the statute sets interest at 9 percent a year with no added penalty. Ask King County Treasury for a current statement before you sign, so the numbers in the contract match what the county shows.

Gather these items before you accept an offer:

  • The deed and your most recent loan payoff statement.
  • Rental registration number and lease copies, if tenants live in the house.
  • Permit records for any ADU, basement unit or addition.
  • The latest King County property tax statement.

More questions about Renton, WA

How fast can I sell my house in Renton, WA?

A cash sale can close as soon as title work is complete, and many sellers choose the date themselves. A listing normally takes longer because it includes showings, inspections and the buyer's financing. Ask any buyer to put the closing date in writing.

Do I need to register my Renton rental before I sell it?

If it is a rental that falls under the program, register or confirm your registration before listing. Renton asks landlords to register annually by January 1, and verified violations must be corrected within 15 days of a warning. Short-term rentals need a business license instead.

Who pays the excise tax on a house sale in Renton?

The seller usually does. The Department of Revenue says the buyer becomes responsible if the seller does not pay, and an unpaid tax can create a lien. The tax is paid to the county treasurer and is calculated from the selling price.

Does the Cedar River flood history affect my sale?

It can, because the disclosure form asks about flooding, drainage problems, floodplains and critical areas. Answer from what you know about your own property, and check current floodplain information for your address before you list.
