The Census Bureau estimates 33,032 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 32,888.

Which school district serves Des Moines?

Most of the city is in Highline Public Schools. The Woodmont and Redondo neighborhoods are in the Federal Way School District. Confirm the district for the exact address.

Yes. The owner needs a city business license and a short-term rental permit, plus a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. A local representative must answer complaints within 30 minutes.

How much is the state excise tax on a $600,000 Des Moines sale?

The state portion is $6,735 under the graduated rates: 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent on the next $75,000. A local rate is added on top, and the seller usually pays.

Is Sea-Tac Airport near Des Moines?

Yes. The airport is about 2 miles north of the city, and some Des Moines property has been bought out because of aircraft noise. Ask the county or an agent about noise context for a specific address.

How can you sell a house fast in Maple Valley, WA?

Maple Valley sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase of the house in its current state. The speed of a cash sale suits a seller who cannot wait through showings, buyer financing and inspection requests. The trade is a price below what a well-prepared listing might bring.

Homes here are valuable and mostly owned by the people who live in them. The Census Bureau estimates the median value of an owner-occupied home in Maple Valley at $724,700, and about 83 percent of homes are owner-occupied. At that price level, sellers should compare what they would net rather than the headline number. Start with this checklist.

  • Payoff figures for the mortgage and any second loan or lien.
  • The cost of repairs an inspector or buyer is likely to raise.
  • Commission and excise tax on a listing, compared with the costs on a direct sale.
  • How many months of payments you can carry while the house sits.

If the house is a rental, a tenant moving out or a lease running past your target date can also decide which route is practical.

What do Census figures show about Maple Valley?

Maple Valley is a family-oriented suburb with high incomes. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts gives these figures for the city.

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 28,482.
  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 9,394, with about 3.01 people each.
  • Persons under 18: 31.3 percent.
  • Median household income: $152,885.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,984.
  • Median gross rent: $2,304.
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 50.2 percent.
  • Mean travel time to work: 37 minutes.

A 37 minute mean commute is the longest among Longview, Lynnwood, Marysville and Maple Valley, so access to State Route 169, State Route 18 and State Route 516 deserves a line in your pitch to a buyer.

How did Maple Valley grow into a Seattle commuter city?

Settlers arrived in 1879, and the early economy ran on coal from Cedar Mountain and Black Diamond, lumber milling and the Northern Pacific rail line. The community took its name from Vine Maple Valley, and the post office shortened it to Maple Valley. Lake Wilderness became a resort lake in the 1920s, with a ballroom, a golf course and rental cabins that operated until 1964. State Route 18, built between Auburn and North Bend in the early 1960s, ran through the city and forced many landmarks to be demolished or moved.

Maple Valley incorporated on August 31, 1997. Because of King County's urban growth boundary, the city is split into sectors along Maple Valley Black Diamond Road (State Route 169). The Four Corners district at State Route 169 and Kent Kangley Road (State Route 516) is the main commercial area, and central Maple Valley is mostly residential. The city covers about 6.2 square miles and borders Covington, Renton, Kent and Black Diamond.

The city's population grew nearly 63 percent from 2000 to 2010, and the 2020 Census counted 28,013 residents. The Green to Cedar River Trail runs through the city, and Lake Wilderness City Park hosts the annual Maple Valley Days Parade each June.

How do the lakes and weather affect a Maple Valley house?

The city has Lake Wilderness, Lake Lucerne, Rock Creek and part of Pipe Lake within its limits, and the Cedar River passes just outside the northeast border. Nights are cooler and rainfall is heavier than in Seattle, and winter days run slightly colder than closer to downtown Seattle. Check the roof, gutters, drainage and crawl space before a buyer's inspector does.

If your property is on or near water, the city asks owners to contact Economic and Community Development before they remove trees, especially on lakefront lots, modify environmentally sensitive areas such as wetlands, slopes and streams, or build or replace a dock. Settle any question about past work with the city before you list.

Which school district serves Maple Valley?

Maple Valley is in the Tahoma School District, whose first school was built here in 1929 and still stands as an elementary school after renovation. Tahoma High School is the school the city names when it discusses local graduates. Confirm the school assignment for your address with the district before you mention it in an ad.

Can you add housing units on a Maple Valley lot?

In many cases, yes. State law, E2SHB 1110, requires cities of Maple Valley's size to allow middle housing on lots zoned mainly for residential use, and the city's FAQ says the requirement applies in its R-4 and R-6 single-family zones. Maple Valley's planning covers duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, townhouses, stacked flats, courtyard apartments and cottage housing, and a property with a single-family home may add two accessory dwelling units for three units total. The state deadline for compliance was June 2025.

Buyers who see development potential may pay attention to your lot size and zoning, so ask the department what your parcel allows before you describe it as a development site.

What state rules apply when you sell in Maple Valley?

RCW 64.06.020 requires most sellers of improved residential real estate to deliver a disclosure statement within five business days after both parties accept a written contract, unless they agree otherwise. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

The Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays the real estate excise tax and that it is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state rate is graduated, and a local rate is added on top. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the thresholds are $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000, with rates of 1.1, 1.28, 2.75 and 3 percent from the lowest band to the highest. Earlier sales use $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. Since the Census median value in Maple Valley is $724,700, a typical sale is taxed partly at 1.1 percent and partly at 1.28 percent.

How do property tax dates and appeals work for a Maple Valley owner?

King County bills the property tax, and state law fixes the schedule. Under RCW 84.56.020, taxes are due on or before April 30, and if you pay half by that date the rest is due by October 31. Residential property with four or fewer units accrues interest at 9 percent a year when delinquent, with no penalties. The statute asks treasurers to send tax statements by March 15 when the budgets and rolls are ready on time.

To dispute an assessed value, RCW 84.40.038 lets you petition the county board of equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the notice, or a longer period up to 60 days if the county has adopted one, whichever is later. The board can waive a late filing for good cause, such as serious illness or a natural disaster. Check your notice for the exact deadline and ask the King County Assessor or Treasury Operations about your account. At closing, the title company usually prorates the current bill.

How should you compare a cash offer in Maple Valley?

Put each offer next to your realistic listing outcome. Subtract commission, excise tax, repair credits and holding costs from the listing price, then subtract the payoff from each side. Ask any cash buyer for the closing date and the costs it expects you to pay in writing, and have a title company or attorney review the contract.

More questions about Maple Valley, WA

Do I need a permit to replace windows in Maple Valley?

Yes. The city's permitting page lists installing new windows or replacing existing ones as work that needs a building permit. Siding replacement and painting do not need one. Call Economic and Community Development at (425) 413-8800 if you are unsure.

What happens if past work on my Maple Valley house had no permit?

It can complicate a sale. The city says unpermitted modifications may require tear-down, vacating or costly repairs, and many lenders want proof of a final inspection. Sellers also have to disclose improvements and whether permits were obtained, so ask the city what is on file.

Can I add accessory dwelling units on a Maple Valley lot?

Often, yes. The city's middle housing FAQ says a property with a single-family home may add two ADUs, for three units total, under the rules adopted to follow state law HB 1110. Zoning and lot details vary, so confirm with the city first.

When are Maple Valley property taxes due?

Taxes are due April 30. If you pay half by then, the second half is due October 31, as RCW 84.56.020 provides. King County sends the bill, and delinquent taxes on residential property with four or fewer units carry 9 percent annual interest.

How do I appeal my assessed value in Maple Valley?

File a petition with the county board of equalization by July 1 or within the number of days stated on your value notice, whichever is later. RCW 84.40.038 sets 30 days, or up to 60 if the county chose that. Include your evidence of value.

Where is Tumwater, and why does its history matter to a house sale?

Tumwater lies in Thurston County about two miles south of Olympia, near the spot where the Deschutes River drops into Budd Inlet at the southern tip of Puget Sound. The city calls itself the end of the Oregon Trail and the oldest permanent American settlement on Puget Sound.

Michael T. Simmons led the first American settlers to Tumwater Falls in 1845, and the settlement was first called New Market before it took the Chinook jargon name for a waterfall by 1863. Tumwater was incorporated as a town on November 25, 1869. The falls powered early sawmills along the river, and the city's history pages still feature the old brewhouse and several historic houses. The Tumwater Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978, preserves what remained of downtown after Interstate 5 opened in 1958 and required the demolition of about 100 buildings.

The 1845 party also included George Bush, whose family settled on the prairies to the south, and the group cut the wagon trail that became the northern branch of the Oregon Trail. If your house is old or sits near the falls, ask the city's Community Development Department at (360) 754-4180 whether any local historic listing or critical area rule touches the lot.

What jobs and schools support demand in Tumwater?

Employers shape who shops for a house here. The city's economic profile, drawn from Thurston County economic development research, lists major employers that include:

  • Home Depot with 341 employees and Fred Meyer with 319.
  • Dart Container with 233, Amcor Rigid Packaging with 150 and Pepsi Northwest Beverages with 140.
  • Cardinal Glass Industries with 100 and Valmet with 94.

The Tumwater School District serves the city, and its high schools include Tumwater High School and Black Hills High School. The city's profile points to the state's school report card for district results. Mean commute time to work is 21.3 minutes, according to the Census Bureau.

The profile's 2022 age table shows 20.9 percent of residents under 18, 18.6 percent aged 25 to 34 and 16.1 percent aged 35 to 44. The same profile counts 27,100 people inside city limits in 2023 and another 2,890 in the urban growth area, for a total of 29,990. Tumwater Square, northeast of the old downtown, remains a local shopping center.

What building and permit rules apply to a Tumwater house?

The City of Tumwater's Community Development Department, through its Building Division, regulates construction, renovations and new building under the Tumwater Municipal Code. The division also conducts building and fire code plan reviews and inspections, and the city has a Development Review Committee that helps decide whether a project is feasible.

Before listing, work through these steps:

  • Pull permit records for any addition, deck, finished basement or mechanical replacement made since you bought.
  • Ask the Building Division how to close an open permit, and call (360) 754-4180 for platting and planned unit development questions.
  • Check zoning, which the city publishes alongside its building codes and development guide.
  • Look at the city's Development Projects interactive map to see which public and private projects are underway near your street.

The city is also asking residents to mark an interactive map of places where more attention is needed for climate resilience planning. In October 2026 Thurston County also urged residents to prepare for fall and winter flooding from major rivers, heavy rain, saturated soils, rising groundwater and overwhelmed drainage systems. If your lot is near the river or a low area, ask the city what the map shows and whether any flood or drainage rule affects the property.

What tax and paperwork steps come with selling in Tumwater?

Thurston County's Treasurer collects property tax for Tumwater parcels from an office at 3000 Pacific Ave SE in Olympia, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and can be reached at 360-786-5550. The first half of the 2026 property tax was due April 30, and the second half was due October 31, with taxpayers given until Monday, November 2 because the 31st fell on a Saturday. Taxes can be paid online, in person, in the drop box in front of the building or by mail, and the county advises mailing early because the post office no longer guarantees same-day postmarks. Both deadlines have passed, so ask the treasurer whether any balance remains before closing.

Real estate excise tax is a separate bill. The seller normally pays it to the county treasurer where the property sits, it is due on the date of sale, and it becomes a lien on the property if nobody pays. State rates start at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price, move to 1.28 percent up to $1,525,000, and add a local portion. Interest accrues once a month passes without payment.

The seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020 covers the roof, foundation, plumbing, electrical system, heating, drainage and more. It must reach the buyer within five business days after the contract is signed on most home sales, and it notes that a seller must provide carbon monoxide alarms and at least one smoke detection device. The statute has the full form.

Is a cash offer a reasonable way to sell a Tumwater house?

It can be, especially when the house needs work or the calendar is tight. A cash buyer in Tumwater takes the house as it stands and has no loan approval to wait for, so the sale does not depend on a lender's appraisal or a repair list.

Weigh these points against a traditional listing:

  • Net proceeds after commission, repairs and carrying costs compared with the cash price.
  • The closing date and whether it matches your move.
  • Who covers the excise tax, title and recording fees.
  • How the buyer treats an open permit, a tenant or items left in the house.

Get any Tumwater offer in writing, and ask a title or escrow company in Thurston County to confirm the payoff and the deed process before you sign.

More questions about Tumwater, WA

How many people live in Tumwater?

The Census Bureau estimates 28,010 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,350 at the April 2020 census and 17,371 in 2010.

Which county handles property tax in Tumwater?

Thurston County does. The Treasurer's office is at 3000 Pacific Ave SE in Olympia and can be reached at 360-786-5550. The 2026 second-half deadline has passed, so ask about any balance before closing.

Who pays real estate excise tax when a Tumwater house sells?

The seller usually pays it to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state portion starts at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and a local portion is added. If it goes unpaid it can become a lien on the property.

Do I need permits closed before selling a Tumwater house?

It is a good idea. Contact the Community Development Department's Building Division at (360) 754-4180 about permits for additions or major systems, and keep the records for the buyer.

What is Tumwater known for?

The city describes itself as the oldest permanent American settlement on Puget Sound and the end of the Oregon Trail. It sits at Tumwater Falls, where the Deschutes River meets Budd Inlet, and it was incorporated in 1869. The climate is a very warm-summer Mediterranean type, with warm, dry summers.

What should I know about selling a house in Camas, WA?

Camas is a Clark County city on the Columbia River, about 20 miles northeast of Portland, with Vancouver on its west side and Washougal on its east. The Census Bureau estimates 27,749 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 6.0 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. Households here are large and incomes are high, and county-level steps run through Clark County offices.

The city was incorporated on June 18, 1906, and takes its name from the camas lily. A paper mill opened in 1883 and shaped the town for more than a century. The mill sits at the west end of downtown and passed to Georgia-Pacific in 2000 and to Koch Industries in 2005. In 2018 Koch announced plans to lay off roughly 200 to 300 workers, and technology employers such as Analog Devices and TSMC Washington now share the local job base.

Camas owner-occupied homes have a median value of $711,700, and 78.3 percent of housing is owner-occupied, per Census Bureau QuickFacts. Values marked 2020-2024 come from the American Community Survey.

Lakes, creeks and Prune Hill shape what buyers see in Camas. Prune Hill, an extinct volcanic vent, rises in the middle of town, and Lacamas Lake, Round Lake, Lacamas Creek, the Washougal River and the Columbia River all lie inside city limits. Lacamas Park runs along State Route 500 with trails around the lakes, and a long list of city parks is scattered through the neighborhoods.

  • Downtown Camas: the historic core near the mill, with the Liberty Theatre and the festival calendar, including Camas Days.
  • Prune Hill: a hillside residential area with a sports park named for it.

Most of Camas belongs to the Camas School District. Small parts of the city lie inside Evergreen Public Schools, so check the district for the address on any listing. Demolition plans for the paper mill have proceeded, with work expected to finish by 2027, and the site is expected to become waterfront on Camas Slough as an extension of the downtown district. Buyers who ask about the neighborhood's direction will likely ask about that project.

Can I sell a Camas house that has an ADU or extra units?

Camas adopted Ordinance 25-025 in 2025 to align with new state housing rules. An accessory dwelling unit is a unit up to 1,000 square feet, attached, detached or a mix, and a lot can have up to two. Camas also allows two middle housing units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable, and it created a unit lot subdivision process that lets parent lots divide into separately owned child lots.

These rules can add value, and they create questions for sellers. ADUs count toward the middle housing total, so a lot with one main home can add two ADUs, while a lot that already holds two middle housing units cannot. Before you list, confirm what was permitted.

  • Permits and inspections run through the city's online system, which has taken applications, inspection requests and status tracking since June 12, 2024.

  • Negotiate a leaseback or delayed possession: helpful when you need time to move after closing.

Ask any buyer for proof of funds and a plain written offer. Then compare the net proceeds, not only the price: the excise tax, payoff of any loan and prorated property taxes all come off the top.

What excise tax and paperwork apply to a Camas sale?

For a deeded transfer in Washington, the excise tax affidavit, the deed and payment go to the county treasurer where the property sits, which for Camas is the Clark County Treasurer. The Department of Revenue says only one exemption can be claimed per transfer and that records must be kept for at least four years. If you overpay, a refund request must be filed within four years of the sale.

The state rate is graduated: 1.1 percent on the portion of the price up to $525,000, 1.28 percent from there to $1,525,000, then higher tiers above that. At $711,700, the Camas median owner-occupied value, the state tax on a sale would be about $8,165 before the local add-on: about $5,775 on the first $525,000 plus about $2,390 on the rest. Treat that as an illustration and ask the escrow officer for the exact bill.

Washington also requires a seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020, delivered within five business days of mutual acceptance unless otherwise agreed. The form covers title, water, sewer, structural and other topics, and the seller is told to sign and date each page. Camas houses near lakes, creeks or slopes should have drainage and septic or sewer details ready, since those questions appear on the form.

How do Clark County property taxes work for a Camas seller?

Clark County collects real property tax in two halves, due April 30 and October 31. The Treasurer says first-half statements are available by March 15 and second-half statements typically by September 15. The second-half 2026 date has passed, and the next due date is April 30, 2027.

For 2023 and later years, late taxes on a residential parcel with four or fewer units accrue 0.75 percent interest per month, with no penalties. The Treasurer accepts mailed payments only if the envelope is postmarked by the due date, and it does not currently accept prepayment of future-year taxes, with exceptions for certain sale transactions such as personal property and mobile homes. Call 564.397.2252 or email treasoff@clark.wa.gov, and ask about the county's tax relief programs for homeowners who meet eligibility requirements.

Up to two. Camas defines an ADU as a unit up to 1,000 square feet, attached or detached. ADUs count toward the middle housing allowance, which is two units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable.

When are Clark County property taxes due?

April 30 for the first half or full year, and October 31 for the second half. Mailed payments need a postmark on or before the due date. Late residential taxes for four or fewer units accrue 0.75 percent per month.

Who collects the excise tax on a Camas home sale?

The county treasurer where the property is located, which for Camas is Clark County. The seller usually pays. The affidavit, deed and payment are submitted together for a deeded transfer.

Which school district serves Camas homes?

Most of the city is in the Camas School District. Small parts of the city limits fall inside Evergreen Public Schools, so confirm the district for the exact address.

Moses Lake is the most populous city in Grant County, and the Census Bureau estimates 27,469 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 20,366 in 2010 and 25,146 in 2020. The city spreads over about 18 square miles of land around a lake with three arms, and the lake sits in the middle of town. How is Moses Lake laid out, and why does the lake matter to a seller?

The lake runs more than 18 miles across its three arms and has over 120 miles of shoreline, so the city has a lot of waterfront property. South of town are Potholes Reservoir and the Columbia National Wildlife Refuge.

The lake was a smaller, shallower body of water until it was dammed in the early 1900s and folded into the Columbia Basin Project. The area had few residents before Moses Lake Army Air Base opened in 1942, and irrigation water from Grand Coulee Dam arrived in 1955. The town of Westlake, platted in 1945 and incorporated in 1958, was annexed into Moses Lake in 1972. Elevation is about 1,060 feet. Public schools belong to the Moses Lake School District, which runs eleven elementary schools, three middle schools, and Moses Lake High School along with several alternative programs.

Which Moses Lake permits can trip up a sale?

Any structure work done without the permit the city requires is the usual problem. The Building Department publishes a list of permit types, and a buyer or title company may ask whether your fence, porch, or roof had one.

  • Fences: a permit is required before installing any fence.
  • Re-roofing: a residential re-roof that replaces more than 25 percent of the sheathing needs a permit, and solar roof panels need one.
  • Retaining walls: a permit applies at 4 feet or higher, measured from the bottom of the footing.
  • Covered porches: a building permit is required for an attached covered porch of 200 square feet or more.
  • Remodels, additions, and accessory dwelling units: submitted through the city's permit portal with plans.
  • Demolition and grading or clearing: each has its own permit.

Call the Moses Lake Building Department at 509-764-3743 if you are unsure about a past project. If something was built without a permit, ask the department how it can be documented before you list.

Can a buyer run a short-term rental in a Moses Lake house?

Only with city approval, and the approval does not follow the house to a new owner. Chapter 15.650 of the Moses Lake Municipal Code regulates stays of less than 30 days and allows them in specified zoning districts.

An owner applies to the Community Development Department for a short-term rental endorsement, and a business license under Chapter 5.04 is not issued until the endorsement is approved. The city says endorsements are generally not transferable, so a buyer who wants to rent the home by the night should expect to apply again after closing. What are the excise tax and recording steps in Moses Lake?

The seller files a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit, pays the tax to the Grant County Treasurer, and the deed is then recorded. The Department of Revenue says the tax is due on the date of sale, which is the date the deed is notarized, even if recording happens later.

The state portion is graduated: 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 under the thresholds in force through December 31, 2026, with 1.28 percent, 2.75 percent, and 3 percent above higher breakpoints. The local rate is added to it. Sales closing in 2027 use breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000, and $3,051,000. The Grant County Treasurer is at 35 C Street NW, Room 204, in Ephrata, phone 509-754-2010, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m. The county's page links the current state affidavit forms for sales on or after May 1, 2026, and it lists April 30 as the deadline for the first half of the year's property taxes. Ask the treasurer how current-year taxes are handled at your closing.

Washington also requires a seller disclosure statement on improved residential property, delivered within five business days of mutual acceptance unless waived or exempt, under RCW 64.06.020.

When does a cash offer make sense in Moses Lake?

It makes sense when the house needs work, a tenant or relative is still inside, or you need a firm closing date. Rentals with worn finishes and inherited homes that nobody wants to renovate are common examples.

Ask any Moses Lake buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and a clear statement of who pays the excise tax and title costs. Request an offer on your Moses Lake address and compare the net to what a listing would leave after excise tax, agent fees, and repairs.

Do I need a permit to sell a Moses Lake house?

No permit is needed to sell. The city requires permits for work such as fences, re-roofs that replace more than 25 percent of the sheathing, retaining walls of 4 feet or more, and covered porches of 200 square feet or more. If past work lacked a permit, contact the Building Department at 509-764-3743 before listing.

Who pays the real estate excise tax in Moses Lake?

The seller usually pays. The Department of Revenue says the buyer is responsible if the seller does not, and unpaid tax can become a lien. It is paid to the Grant County Treasurer on the date of sale, with the local rate added to the state's graduated rate.

Does a short-term rental permit transfer to the buyer in Moses Lake?

Generally no. Moses Lake issues short-term rental endorsements under Chapter 15.650, and the city says they are generally not transferable, so a new owner may need a new endorsement before renting by the night.

How much state excise tax would a $310,000 Moses Lake sale owe?

The state portion is $3,410, which is 1.1 percent of $310,000. That figure is the Census median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024. The local excise tax is added, so ask your title officer for the full amount.

Grant County handles both. The treasurer collects the excise tax and links the Department of Revenue affidavit forms, and Washington law requires deeds to be recorded with the county auditor. Call the treasurer at 509-754-2010 to confirm what to bring.

What are Mountlake Terrace's neighborhoods and boundaries?

  • Town Center: between 220th and 236th streets, with retailers, restaurants, and civic buildings near Veterans Memorial Park.
  • Cedar Terrace: east of the Town Center and Terrace Creek Park, mostly residential with apartments along Cedar Way.
  • Cascade View: the north side from Interstate 5 east to Brier, including the high school campus.

  • Lake Ballinger and Melody Hill: the remaining two planning neighborhoods. Lake Ballinger is a 100-acre lake in the southwest that drains toward Lake Washington.

Name the neighborhood in your listing or cash offer request. It tells buyers which schools, roads, and transit stops apply.

How do commuters and employers shape Mountlake Terrace?

Most residents work elsewhere. In 2018 figures, only 3.2 percent of employed residents worked inside city limits, and 37.0 percent commuted to Seattle. The largest employer is Premera Blue Cross, with 2,446 employees in 2022.

Interstate 5 has interchanges at State Route 104 (244th Street Southwest), 236th Street Southwest, and 220th Street Southwest, and State Route 99 touches the western edge. The Mountlake Terrace transit station, which opened in 2009, has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the line to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Community Transit runs local routes to Edmonds, Lynnwood, and Brier, and King County Metro serves the station from Shoreline, Lake Forest Park, and Kenmore. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute for city residents at 27.9 minutes, a number worth quoting in your listing.

Who provides schools and utilities in Mountlake Terrace?

Public schools belong to the Edmonds School District, which has five schools inside the city: one high school, one middle school, and three elementary schools. Mountlake Terrace High School opened in 1960, was rebuilt in 1991 on the same campus, and sits in the northeast corner of the city.

  • Electricity: Snohomish County Public Utility District.
  • Natural gas: Puget Sound Energy.
  • Water and sewer: Alderwood Water and Wastewater District.
  • Garbage, recycling, and yard waste: collected under city contract with Waste Management.

Tell buyers which providers serve the house so they can price the monthly bills.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Mountlake Terrace houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What permit rules matter when you sell a Mountlake Terrace house?

Work done without a permit is the main risk. The city's permit FAQ says failing to get one before construction is a code violation that can bring fines, that you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or restore the site, and that permit fees may be doubled as a penalty.

  • Window and siding installation, roofing, plumbing, electrical, and structural changes always need a permit.
  • Sheds over 80 square feet or over 6 feet high need one, and a garage turned into living space is a change of use that needs one.
  • Removing drywall and exposing framing needs one, even for a wall removal or remodel.
  • Like-for-like cabinet replacement, painting, and carpet do not.
  • Permits expire if work does not start and pass an inspection within 180 days.

The FAQ adds that an owner doing the work must live in the home, and that a contractor is required if you plan to rent or sell. Email the permit specialists at permitspecialist@mltwa.gov for a specific project, and check the posted counter hours before you visit.

What are the excise tax and recording steps in Snohomish County?

The Snohomish County Treasurer reviews the deed first, and the Auditor's Recording Division records it second. If excise tax is owed, the deed cannot be recorded until it is paid in full at the Treasurer's excise tax counter.

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., phone 425-388-3366, at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett. Recording is in the same building, open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone 425-388-3483, and mail submissions need the exact recording fee. Recording fees depend on document type and page count.

The state tax is graduated at 1.1, 1.28, 2.75, and 3 percent by price slice, with the first breakpoint at $525,000 through December 31, 2026 and $551,000 from January 1, 2027. The local rate is added, and the tax is due on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue treats as the notarization date. The seller disclosure statement in RCW 64.06.020 is due within five business days of mutual acceptance unless waived or exempt.

When does a cash offer make sense in Mountlake Terrace?

It makes sense when the house needs updating, when a probate or move is on a deadline, or when you want to avoid repairs a buyer's lender would require. Older houses with deferred updates are a typical fit.

Ask any buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and who pays the excise tax and title fees. Then compare the offer against a listing's net after excise tax, agent fees, repairs, and carrying costs. Request an offer on your Mountlake Terrace address to see the numbers side by side.

More questions about Mountlake Terrace, WA

Can I sell a Mountlake Terrace house that has unpermitted work?

Yes, but expect it to come up. The city says work without a permit is a code violation, and you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or return the site to its original condition. Ask the permit specialists about your case before listing, or sell to a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

Who records the deed for a Mountlake Terrace sale?

Snohomish County does. The Treasurer's Office reviews conveyance documents such as deeds for excise tax, and the Auditor's Recording Division records them after any tax is paid. Recording is at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett, phone 425-388-3483.

How much state excise tax would a $667,300 Mountlake Terrace sale owe?

The state portion is $7,596.44: $5,775 on the first $525,000 at 1.1 percent and $1,821.44 on the remaining $142,300 at 1.28 percent. The local excise tax is added, and sales closing after January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints.

Which school district serves Mountlake Terrace?

The Edmonds School District. Five of its schools are inside the city: Mountlake Terrace High School, one middle school, and three elementary schools. Confirm your attendance area with the district before you advertise a school assignment.

Does the light rail station affect selling a Mountlake Terrace house?

It gives you a transit selling point. The Mountlake Terrace station has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the extension to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Mention the station and the commute time when you describe the house.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Mercer Island?
We buy Mercer Island houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How does selling a house in Mercer Island work?

You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes it as-is. Each route ends the same way: a deed, an excise tax affidavit, and a recording with King County.

Mercer Island sits in the southern half of Lake Washington, with Seattle to the west and Bellevue to the east. The city limits match the island, which is about six miles long and up to four miles wide. The Census Bureau counts 25,422 residents as of July 1, 2025, living on 6.38 square miles of land, and the island has its own hazard maps, permit rules, and school district, all covered below.

A cash sale suits owners who do not want to schedule showings, finish repairs, or wait for a buyer to line up financing. Listing can bring a higher price when the house is clean, permitted, and ready for photos. The rest of this page covers the numbers and city rules that decide which route fits.

What do Census figures say about Mercer Island homeowners?

Mercer Island is an owner-heavy, high-value city: 67.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the Census Bureau lists the median owner-occupied value at $2,000,000 or more. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $219,069, and median gross rent is $2,502.

  • Households: 10,068, averaging 2.50 people each.
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.2 percent, so inherited and downsizing sales are common.
  • Living in the same house one year earlier: 86.8 percent, which points to long ownership.
  • Mean commute: 23.6 minutes.

If you have owned the house for a long time, pull its permit history before you list. It shows which additions and remodels the city has on file.

How much state excise tax does a Mercer Island seller owe?

Washington charges a graduated real estate excise tax on the sale price, and the seller usually pays it. For a $2,000,000 sale under the thresholds that apply through December 31, 2026, the state portion comes to $31,637.50.

Slice of a $2,000,000 priceState rateTax
First $525,0001.10%$5,775.00
$525,000 to $1,525,0001.28%$12,800.00
$1,525,000 to $2,000,0002.75%$13,062.50
State total$31,637.50

Source: RCW 82.45.060 and the Department of Revenue REET page. Sales that close on or after January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.

The Department of Revenue says the local REET is added on top of the state amount. Ask your title officer for the exact local rate on your closing date. The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, which the department treats as the day the deed is notarized, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Mercer Island house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Do slope and seismic maps affect a Mercer Island sale?

They can. The city maps four hazard areas on its GIS portal: seismic, steep slope, erosion, and potential slide. If your lot is in one of them, work on the ground or vegetation usually needs a permit, and buyers will ask about it.

The island formed as a glacial plateau with ravines, and its elevation runs from about 18 feet at the lake shore to about 394 feet near Rotary Park. The Seattle Fault crosses the northern part of the island. On lots flagged as erosion, potential slide, or steep slope, the city does not allow clearing, grading, filling, or foundation work between October 1 and April 1 unless a waiver is granted with a geotechnical evaluation. A geotechnical report from a Washington licensed engineer is required when a structure goes into a critical area.

If you plan a repair before selling, check the map first. A retaining wall or deck fix that would be exempt on flat ground can need review on a slope.

Do unpermitted projects matter when you sell on Mercer Island?

Yes. The city's Code Compliance planner handles work done without required permits, and a buyer's lender or inspector can ask about past remodels. The city's own rule is that exemption from a building permit does not exempt a project from building or land use codes.

Under MICC 17.14.010, a permit covers work that builds, enlarges, alters, repairs, moves, demolishes, or changes the use of a structure, and it covers electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems. The city lists 22 exceptions. Examples include:

  • One-story detached sheds, playhouses, and similar structures up to 200 square feet.
  • Fences up to 6 feet high.
  • Retaining walls up to 4 feet, measured from the bottom of the footing, on flat ground with no surcharge.
  • Decks and driveways not more than 30 inches above grade and not over a basement.
  • In-kind re-roofing where the sheathing is not replaced.

Those exceptions do not apply in flood hazard areas or critical areas unless the work is entirely inside an existing legal building. The city also lists accessory dwelling units, tree cutting without a permit, and vacant unsecured structures among its code compliance topics. Construction hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Friday and 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday, with no work on Sundays or holidays.

What paperwork does a Mercer Island seller handle?

You complete a seller disclosure statement, sign a deed, and file a real estate excise tax affidavit. The disclosure is due within five business days of mutual acceptance unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies, and the buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind.

The statutory form in RCW 64.06.020 asks about title, easements, boundary disputes, assessments, zoning violations, water, sewer, and structural problems. Answer from what you actually know and attach explanations for any yes answer.

  • King County Assessor: property report with lot size, present use, and year built.
  • King County Recorder's Office: recorded plats, surveys, and deeds.
  • MyBuildingPermit.com: status of building and land use permits.
  • City Online Map Portal: permit files, sewer as-builts, and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
  • Residential certificate of occupancy: for most island houses, the permit card with the signed final inspection serves as the certificate.

The City of Mercer Island permit center is at 9611 SE 36th Street, and land use staff take calls at 206-275-7605.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Mercer Island houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What do schools, bridges and transit look like on Mercer Island?

The Mercer Island School District runs seven schools on the island: Lakeridge, Island Park, West Mercer, and Northwood elementaries, Islander Middle School, Mercer Island High School, and the Crest Learning Center. Enrollment was 3,993 students in 2024 to 2025.

Interstate 90 crosses the island on the Lacey V. Murrow and Homer M. Hadley floating bridges toward Seattle and on the East Channel Bridge toward Bellevue. Much of the freeway is covered by the Mercer Island Lid, which holds parks and the Mountains to Sound Greenway trail. Sound Transit's 2 Line station in the I-90 median opened on March 28, 2026 and has a park-and-ride with 447 stalls. The city maintains 75 miles of streets, and Puget Sound Energy supplies electricity and natural gas.

These details help when you write a listing or explain the property to a cash buyer, since the island has one freeway corridor and a short list of schools.

When does a cash offer make sense for a Mercer Island house?

A cash offer makes sense when time, condition, or paperwork would slow a listing. Inherited houses, homes with deferred repairs, properties with old permit gaps, and sales with tenants in place are the usual cases.

Compare the net, not the headline price. On a listing, subtract the state and local excise tax, any agent fee you agree to, repair credits, and carrying costs such as utilities and insurance during the weeks the house sits. On a cash sale, ask the buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and who pays the excise tax and title costs. Then request an offer on your Mercer Island address and weigh it against the list-and-wait numbers.

More questions about Mercer Island, WA

Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Mercer Island house sells?

The seller usually pays it. The Department of Revenue says the buyer becomes responsible if the seller does not, and unpaid tax can create a lien. The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the local rate is added to the graduated state rate.

Can I sell a Mercer Island house with work that was never permitted?

Yes, but expect questions. The city's Code Compliance planner handles work without required permits, and the usual fix is a courtesy letter or correction notice that asks you to resolve the issue. A cash buyer may take the house as it stands, while a listing buyer's inspector or lender may ask for the permit history.

Does the seller disclosure form apply to every Mercer Island sale?

It applies to improved residential property unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt under RCW 64.06.010. The seller delivers it within five business days of mutual acceptance unless the parties agree otherwise, and the buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.

Does a steep or low-lying lot change how I sell on Mercer Island?

It can. The city maps seismic, steep slope, erosion, and potential slide hazards. Permit exemptions that apply on flat lots do not apply in critical areas, and ground work on erosion, slide, or steep slope lots is limited between October 1 and April 1 unless the city grants a waiver.

Where do I find recorded deeds and the sale history for my Mercer Island property?

Use the King County Recorder's Office for recorded plats, surveys, and deeds, and the King County Assessor for values and sales history. The city's Online Map Portal also shows permit files and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
